newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian union approves deal with Chrysler.
newsitem.headline: Canadian union approves deal with Chrysler.

text.p: An overwhelming 85 percent of Chrysler Canada Ltd. workers participating in a ratification vote on Sunday voted in favor of a three-year contract that limits the company's ability to contract out jobs.
About 42 percent of the 12,600 unionized members of the Chrysler Corp. unit's Canadian workforce turned out for the vote, officials at the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) union said.

The result, widely expected after CAW president Buzz Hargrove urged the 3,500 workers at company's assembly plants to accept the offer, sets the stage for talks with the local subsidiaries of the other two Big Three carmakers.

"Workers and their communities deserve to share in the success of the corporations -- this contract recognizes the contribution that workers have made to that success," Hargrove said while while announcing the result.
Hargrove has said the CAW will announce Monday if it will next target Ford Motor Co. or General Motors Corp..
Talks with GM, which is trying to outsource more of its production, are expected to be tough.

The deal with Chrysler, reached in a last-minute session ahead of a strike deadline Tuesday, provides for about 300 new jobs and wage increases and projected cost-of-living allowances totaling 10.2 percent over three years.
Chrysler has said it will replace any job it contracts out with a similar job at one of its plants. It has also promised not to sell or close any plants over the life of the contract.
The union will use the Chrysler deal as a blueprint for talks with Ford and GM in a strategy called pattern bargaining, used by the CAW and its U.S. counterpart, the United Autoworkers, for decades.
The UAW earlier this month settled recently with Ford, which makes it likely that the CAW will choose GM as its next target.
